name: LP auto-solve to target rates
description: You enter target items and rates; a linear-programming solver chooses which recipes to run and how many machines of each, minimising some cost.
data_supported: yes — recipes, durations, ingredients/products and producers are all in Docs (872 FGRecipe); fluid amounts are stored x1000 (Plastic: crude Amount=3000 = 3 m³)
notes: observed (repos/sites). SCIM's planner also computes chains but its method could not be verified (Cloudflare 403), so it is not listed here. The baseline every serious tool has. FP's 'matrix solver' is optional; Foreman2/YAFC use OR-Tools; FactorioLab GLPK; FICSIT Planner and dsp-calc-opt HiGHS-WASM; SatisfactoryTools solves server-side.

name: Recursive tree expansion (no optimiser)
description: Each item is made by one chosen recipe and the tool expands ingredients recursively to the target rate; no optimisation, no global balancing.
notes: observed. Simplest model; breaks on recipe loops and shared byproducts (Alchemy calc README admits 'recursive loop calculations and the weirdness'). Factory Manager combines shared intermediates on top of it.

name: Manual node graph with rate propagation
description: The user places recipe/splitter/merger nodes and wires them; the tool propagates rates through the user-built graph but never chooses recipes itself.
notes: observed (SA inferred from source). Ficsit Companion's author rejects auto-planning on purpose ('takes away part of the fun'). Distinct from the LP solver: the user owns the structure.

name: Splitter/merger behaviour simulation
description: Simulates how in-game splitters and mergers actually divide and combine flow (including priority splitters), so a drawn layout's real throughput is computed, not the ideal ratio.
data_supported: partial — buildings exist in Docs, but split/merge behaviour is game logic, not data
notes: observed. Modeler's headline differentiator ('no other Satisfactory planning tool can do'). Reviews say it is slow on large builds and lacks custom split ratios (reported, vaporlens).

name: Manual ledger with satisfy/trim sizing
description: The user sets quantities by hand; the tool reports each shortfall or surplus and offers buttons that size a row exactly to need or to supplier capacity, naming the number it will set.
notes: observed (spreadsheets reported: refactory is listed as 'spreadsheet-like tool for manual decision-making'). Satisfactory Factories has no solver at all; this is its alternative. Buttons show their result ('Trim (480)') before you press.

name: Maximize output under limits
description: Instead of a target rate, maximise production of one or more items (optionally in fixed ratios) subject to resource or recipe limits.
notes: observed (SatisfactoryTools 'max' production type; FactorioLab Maximize+Limit objectives). Satisfactory-Optimizer inferred from description. Needs limits or the LP is unbounded — FactorioLab explains this in-app.

name: Scale targets to a pinned input
description: Type how much of a raw resource you actually have and the targets scale to consume exactly that.
notes: observed (FICSIT Planner README claim; FactorioLab 'Input' objective = 'I am already producing this quantity'). Kirk's 2019 request 'calculate based on input rate' is still open (absence not verified in source).

name: Use on-hand / external supply
description: Mark items that arrive from elsewhere (another factory, a train) so the plan consumes them rather than building their chain.
notes: observed. dsp-calc-opt models it as negative demand; Alchemy calc as 'external input toggles'; Satisfactory Logistics Map uses actual factory surplus from the save.

name: Per-resource caps
description: Set a per-minute maximum for each raw resource (default: the whole map's supply) that the plan may not exceed.
data_supported: partial — the default 'whole map' cap needs node counts and purities, which are world data not in Docs
notes: observed. Every tool hardcodes map totals; SCIM's node data is licence-locked against reuse.

name: Resource scarcity weighting
description: Weights in the objective so the solver prefers abundant resources and spares scarce ones (or treats all equally).
data_supported: partial — weights are usually derived from map totals (not in Docs)
notes: observed. Kirk uses drag-to-rank priority; SatisfactoryTools 'resourceWeight'; FICSIT Planner 'spare scarce first' vs 'All equal'. SatisfactoryTools issue notes weights not derived from max (2020).

name: Selectable optimisation goal
description: Choose what 'best' means — fewest buildings, least power, least raw resource, smallest footprint — and get a different plan.
data_supported: yes for power/buildings/resources; partial for footprint (mClearanceData boxes)
notes: observed. Satisfactory Logistics shows 'compact' vs 'power-efficient' side by side with a summary panel to compare methods.

name: Solver cost tuning
description: Expose the solver's penalty weights (surplus, unproduceable item, excluded item, machine count, footprint, recipe cost) to the user.
notes: observed. Power-user feature; FactorioLab is the only one surfacing it.

name: Infeasibility diagnostics
description: When no plan exists, say why — which limit is too tight, which recipe makes a maximise unbounded, which ticked alternate was kept out.
notes: observed. SatisfactoryMCP reports 'infeasible instead of overstated' when byproducts would be stranded; dsp-calc-opt falls back to the last good recipe set on failure. Users of SatisfactoryTools report silent nonsense instead (issue: calculator 'create diamonds for no reason', 2026-05).

name: Byproduct handling
description: Account for secondary outputs: feed them back in, route them to a sink, package them, or flag them as unhandled (which would back up and stop machines in game).
data_supported: yes — products lists include byproducts; sink points per item in Docs
notes: observed. Satisfactory Factories warns 'byproduct nothing consumes will back up'; Factory Manager adds optional disposal lines; SatisfactoryTools has 'sinkable resources'. Heavy Oil Residue / waste chains are where tools are reported wrong (SatisfactoryTools and SCIM planner issues).

name: Recipe loops and recursive recipes
description: Correctly solve chains where an item is (directly or indirectly) an ingredient of itself — recycled rubber/plastic, fuel loops, self-fertilising farms.
notes: observed. YAFC exists because Helmod broke on recursive Pyanodon recipes; FactorioLab 'net production only'. SatisfactoryTools has an open issue about the rubber/plastic loop (2024-12).

name: Whole-machine counts and clock spreading
description: Turn fractional machine counts into buildable whole numbers with a clock speed (e.g. 3 machines at 83.3%), or spread a group so every machine runs identically.
notes: observed. Satisfactory Factories 'Spread' (fewest buildings, underclocked evenly); dsp-calc-opt mixes machine tiers to reach even counts; Modeler 'automatic clock speed' (2025-08). SatisfactoryTools prints 'N x at Y%' with only the last machine underclocked (RecipeResult.ts).

name: Pause or manual recalculation
description: Stop automatic recomputation while editing a large plan and recompute on demand.
notes: observed. Exists because large graphs freeze — Modeler's top complaint is performance on big builds (reported).

name: Undo / redo
description: Step back and forward through edits to a plan.
notes: observed for YAFC; inferred for Satisfactory Architect (StateHistory.svelte.ts). Satisfactory Factories offers browser back/forward for navigation jumps, not edit undo.

name: Alternate recipe toggles
description: Enable or disable each alternate (and standard) recipe so the planner may or may not use it.
data_supported: yes — 110 Recipe_Alternate classes; 109 EST_Alternate schematics link them
notes: observed (SCIM reported via search snippet; Modeler reported). Table stakes. SatisfactoryTools users ask to 'permanently mark unlocked alts' (open, 2025-03).

name: Converter recipe switch
description: Exclude or include the Converter's resource-transmutation recipes as a group (they make almost anything from SAM and distort optimal plans).
notes: observed. SatisfactoryTools has an open request to disable them by default (2024-10).

name: Progression gating (tier / research)
description: Pick your unlocked tier or research and hide recipes, buildings, belts and miners you cannot have yet.
data_supported: yes — FGSchematic mTechTier, mUnlocks, mSchematicDependencies (574 schematics)
notes: observed. FactorioLab 'technologies researched' with import; YAFC 'milestones'; Satisfactory Logistics 'building restrictions'. SatisfactoryTools request to filter by HUB tier is open (2025-09).

name: Unlocked recipes read from a save
description: Read which alternates and milestones you actually own from your save file and restrict the planner to them.
data_supported: partial — needs a save parser; Docs maps schematics to recipes
notes: observed. Requested on SatisfactoryTools since 2021-03 (open, 10 comments) and on SCIM planner (2022, closed — outcome not verified).

name: Alternate recipe comparison
description: Compare the ways of making an item side by side (raw cost, power, buildings) to decide which alternate is better.
notes: observed. Kirk's request 'alternate recipes best in categories' open since 2020. YAFC's 'Never Enough Items' shows which option it considers optimal.

name: Hard drive research advisor
description: Given the alternates offered by a pending hard drive, recommend which to pick for your goals.
data_supported: partial — alternates are in Docs; the offered choices live in the save
notes: observed for SatisfactoryMCP (advise_hard_drive_pick); reported for SCIM, where only the homepage label 'hard drive optimizer' was seen and its function was not verified. Unusual.

name: Recipe swap from the graph or row
description: Click a machine or row and switch it to another recipe for the same product without leaving the view.
notes: observed. Open request on SatisfactoryTools (2026-05).

name: Game-mode multipliers (1.2)
description: Apply 1.2 game-mode settings: recipe parts cost multiplier, power consumption multiplier, Space Elevator deliverable cost multiplier.
data_supported: partial — fields exist (FGGameState.h mPartsCostMultiplier, mEnergyCostMultiplier, mSpacePartsCostMultiplier) but which recipes are exempt (packagers, generators, diluted fuel) is community knowledge
notes: observed. FactorioLab needed follow-up fixes for exemptions (2026-08-16 generators, 2026-09-17 diluted packaged fuel). Kirk issue open (2026-04). New since June 2026, so a freshness test for any tool.

name: Seasonal content toggle
description: Include or hide event-only (FICSMAS) items and recipes.
notes: observed. Kirk issue 'Ficmas Recipes' open (2024-12).

name: Mod content support
description: Plan with recipes and buildings added by mods, not only vanilla.
data_supported: no — CommunityResources is vanilla only; mods need their own data (ContentLib JSON etc.)
notes: observed (SCIM '93 mods'; Modeler 'mod support via file editing' reported). For Factorio it is the main reason YAFC/Foreman/Helmod exist.

name: User-editable recipe database
description: Edit or add items and recipes in the tool itself (stored locally) to fix data errors or add content.
notes: observed. For Alchemy Factory it is a necessity: no official data dump, recipes are hand-transcribed. FactorioLab has a full game-data editor.

name: Game version switcher
description: Choose which game version's data the plan uses (e.g. 1.0 vs 1.2, experimental vs stable).
data_supported: partial — we hold one Docs snapshot (1.2); older versions would need archived dumps
notes: observed. Foreman2 can diff two presets to show what an update changed. SatisfactoryTools users ask for 1.0 not 0.8 as default (2025-11).

name: Overclock / underclock per machine
description: Set a machine's clock speed (1–250%) and get the scaled rate and the game's non-linear power draw.
notes: observed (Kirk: per-recipe overclock in factory.js/display.js, so its 2019 issues are stale; SCIM power planner reported). SatisfactoryTools: codex views apply an overclock slider, but the production planner does not let you set clocks and its power total says 'TODO handle overclocking' (ProductionToolResult.ts:67). The planner request has been open since 2022.

name: Power shard count and budget
description: Count the power shards a plan needs and optionally plan within a shard budget (prefer 100% clocks).
data_supported: yes — mPotentialShardSlots and potential bounds on each building
notes: observed. Kirk: a request has been open since 2019, but absence was not verified in source.

name: Somersloop production amplification
description: Model somersloops in a machine: up to double output, with power scaling by the square of the boost.
notes: observed (Kirk: maxSomersloop in building.js, used by solve.js). The most-requested missing feature on SatisfactoryTools: three open issues 2024–2026, and grep for 'somersloop' over its 157 source files found nothing (control: the same grep found 'overclock'). Satisfactory Logistics shipped a per-machine display fix in v0.10.

name: Auto-place a limited somersloop supply
description: Enter how many somersloops you own and let the planner place them where they save the most.
notes: observed (README claim). Open request on SatisfactoryTools (2025-07, 'with best-recipe selection').

name: Research and upgrade levels
description: Account for researched bonuses that change rates (belt speed, machine efficiency, mining productivity, upload rate).
data_supported: partial — Satisfactory has few such bonuses; Depot upload research is in MAM schematics
notes: observed. Mostly a non-Satisfactory need (Alchemy Factory belt/efficiency tiers; Factorio mining productivity). Satisfactory Factories models the Dimensional Depot MAM upload tiers.

name: Modules, beacons, proliferators, quality
description: Game-specific machine modifiers (Factorio modules, beacons and quality; DSP proliferator), with presets and auto-allocation.
data_supported: n-a — no Satisfactory equivalent beyond shards/sloops
notes: observed. Relevant only if the multi-game ambition includes Factorio or DSP. YAFC 'auto modules' and dsp-calc-opt proliferator optimisation are the advanced forms.

name: Plan power total
description: Total power a plan consumes, as average and as peak.
notes: observed. Kirk shows both average and peak.

name: Variable-power machines
description: Handle machines whose draw cycles (Particle Accelerator, Converter, Quantum Encoder) as min/max/average instead of a constant.
notes: inferred (Kirk's average-vs-peak split is the visible sign; others not checked). Note the game's own typo 'Mininum' in the field name.

name: Power plant planner
description: Size generators from a MW target or from available fuel, including the fuel chain, water and waste (nuclear).
data_supported: yes — FGBuildableGeneratorFuel mFuel (fuel, supplemental water ratio, byproduct), mPowerProduction
notes: observed (SCIM reported). Kirk: its data lists no fuel generators, only the Nuclear Power Plant (inferred: no power-plant planner). Fuel amounts for fluids are x1000 in Docs. Nuclear waste is where tools break: SatisfactoryTools 'plutonium fuel rod error' open since 2022.

name: Self-powered factory
description: Fold the generators and fuel needed to power a plan into the plan itself, so power reduces to raw resources.
notes: observed. Satisfactory Factories 'match generator draw to fuel supply' (Expand/Trim to supply).

name: Power balance per factory or group
description: Show generated vs consumed vs balance per factory, per group and per plan, with deficit warnings.
data_supported: yes for planned; no for live (needs save or FRM)
notes: observed.

name: Power augmenter boost
description: Model the Alien Power Augmenter's grid-wide percentage boost.
notes: observed. Niche; Satisfactory Factories notes the boost applies to the whole plan's grid.

name: Extractor sizing by mark, purity and clock
description: Compute how many miners/pumps/extractors a raw demand needs, given miner mark, node purity and clock speed.
data_supported: partial — base extractor rates in Docs (fluid extractors x1000: water pump 2000/cycle = 120 m³/min); purity multipliers (0.5/1/2) are hardcoded in every tool (only the enum is in FGResourceNode.h)
notes: observed. SatisfactoryTools hardcodes RESOURCE_MULTIPLIER_IMPURE=0.5 etc. in Constants.ts. Water extractors are a frequent omission (SatisfactoryTools issue open 2021).

name: Node inventory input
description: Enter the nodes you actually have (e.g. one pure, one impure) and get miners per node, or what would close a shortfall per purity.
notes: observed.

name: Resource well planning
description: Plan Resource Well Pressurizers with satellite extractors of mixed purity for water, oil and nitrogen.
data_supported: yes — FGBuildableFrackingExtractor and FGBuildableFrackingActivator in Docs
notes: observed. Satisfactory Factories deliberately won't auto-size wells because rate comes from satellites.

name: Raw resources must be sourced
description: Treat raw resources like any other input that must be explicitly mined or imported, instead of assuming unlimited free supply.
notes: observed. A breaking change in Satisfactory Factories v0.6, with a wizard to migrate plans. A definitional choice worth deciding early: most LP tools assume free raw supply up to a cap.

name: Hand-gathered items
description: Recognise items no extractor can produce (leaves, wood, mycelia, alien remains, slugs) and treat them as gathered.
data_supported: yes — derivable: items with no recipe and no allowed extractor
notes: observed. YAFC's 'automation analysis' is the general form ('cannot be fully automated').

name: Belt and pipe sizing
description: For each flow, show how many belts or pipes of which tier it needs, and split a flow that exceeds one belt.
data_supported: yes with conversion — belt mSpeed/2 = items/min (Mk1 120→60 … Mk6 2400→1200); pipe mFlowLimit×60 = m³/min (5→300, 10→600)
notes: observed. Factory Manager caps the highest Mk you have unlocked.

name: Splitter and balancer design
description: Given a flow and a desired split, produce the splitter/merger arrangement (manifold, balancer or compressor).
notes: observed (Balancer Calculator reported). SCIM publishes a balancer design library; Satisfactory Logistics added a splitter calculator in v0.11; Factory Manager splits steps into manifold banks.

name: Manifold fill time
description: Estimate how long a manifold takes to saturate all machines after start-up.
data_supported: partial — needs machine buffer sizes and belt speed
notes: reported (wiki listing; stale, Update 2 only). Unusual.

name: Transport capacity planning
description: For an inter-factory route, pick trains, trucks, drones or fluid trucks, enter distance or times, and get vehicles, wagons and stations needed.
data_supported: partial — vehicles, platforms and their timings are in Docs; travel speeds and round trips need distance and physics assumptions
notes: observed (Satisfactory Logistics 'Transport & Logistics graph' reported). Missing from Modeler (reported, vaporlens). SatisfactoryBase updates route capacity as you move waypoints.

name: Factory-to-factory import/export ledger
description: Track what each factory sends to and receives from every other factory, and whether the supplier can actually cover it.
notes: observed. Satisfactory Factories offers 'Trim to capacity'. Satisfactory Logistics was built around this ('logistics tracking').

name: Multiple factories per plan
description: Hold many factories (tabs or cards) in one plan or workspace instead of a single production target.
notes: observed. FactorioLab does it by saved states, not a linked network.

name: Nested sub-plans
description: A recipe or block can contain its own sub-plan (subfloor, nested table, outpost, blueprint) that collapses to a summary.
notes: observed. A different structure from a network of sibling factories; Factory Planner nests infinitely. On the Alchemy calc roadmap ('modules').

name: Factory groups with rollups
description: Group factories into coloured folders whose headers summarise what the group delivers, its power and its problems.
notes: observed.

name: Spin off a sub-chain
description: From a shortage or an item row, create a new factory or window that plans just that item, linked back as an import.
notes: observed.

name: Plan statistics and building summary
description: Plan-wide totals: raw resources, every item's production vs consumption, building counts by type, shards and sloops used.
notes: observed.

name: Construction bill of materials
description: Parts needed to build all the machines and generators in a plan.
data_supported: yes — 549 build-gun recipes (BP_BuildGun) give building costs
notes: observed. Satisfactory Factories excludes belts and foundations and labels the figure a guide.

name: Plan health warnings
description: Severity-coded warnings: shortage, unmet export, overproduction/backlog, unhandled byproduct, out of sync with game, redundant import.
notes: observed. Foreman2 colours nodes (red unachievable, gold overproducing, orange error) and offers click-to-auto-resolve.

name: Space Elevator phase targets
description: Use Space Elevator phase deliverables as plan targets or show what remains for a phase.
data_supported: partial — milestone costs (mCost) are in Docs; 'Project Assembly' phase data present but its structure not verified
notes: observed. Interacts with the 1.2 Space Elevator cost multiplier.

name: Non-producing buildings in plan
description: Add buildings that make nothing (portals, stations, radar, AWESOME Sink) so their power and consumption (e.g. portal Singularity Cells) count.
notes: observed.

name: AWESOME Sink planning
description: Route surpluses to sinks and count sink points per minute; sinks draw power.
notes: observed. Sink points are also the natural 'profit' metric if mirroring Alchemy Factory's profit view.

name: Dimensional Depot uploads
description: Model uploads to the Dimensional Depot as a destination, with the MAM-researched upload rate.
data_supported: partial — FGCentralStorageContainer present (mTimeToUpload); rate tiers come from MAM research
notes: observed. SCIM's Depot support (2026-08 commits) edits Depot values in a save; that is save editing, not planning, so it is not listed here.

name: Storage buffers in model
description: Model storage containers or fluid buffers as nodes with a fill state that can supply or absorb flow.
notes: observed.

name: Build checklist
description: Tick off steps, machines or imports as built in-game, and see when the plan changed after you ticked.
notes: observed. Satisfactory Factories flags 'desynced' ticks when the number moved. The 'done state on visualisation' is SatisfactoryTools' second-most-discussed open request (2024-10, 2026-03).

name: Kanban build status
description: Give each factory a status (Draft, Todo, In Progress, Done) and view the megabase on a drag-and-drop board.
notes: observed (v0.10). Paired with 'disabled factory' archiving.

name: Notes and tasks per factory
description: Free-text notes and a task list attached to a factory.
notes: observed. SCIM's save editor has a Map/Todo modal (inferred from file name), but whether it is per factory is unknown, so it is not listed here. Requested on Modeler's forum ('Notes and Checklists').

name: Plan vs save diff
description: Compare a plan with what is actually built in the save: what is missing, what is extra.
notes: observed (diff_vs_save, commission_plan). Unique in this survey.

name: Flow graph with auto layout
description: Show the plan as nodes (machines or recipes) and edges (item flows) laid out automatically.
notes: observed (Satisfactory Architect inferred; SatisGraphtory reported, stale since 2023). SatisfactoryTools and FactorioLab use ELK; Satisfactory Logistics offers orthogonal edges and animated flow dots.

name: Sankey diagram
description: Show flows as a Sankey diagram, with band width proportional to rate.
notes: observed (Sankey Factory reported). Kirk added Sankey alignment as a 2026 issue request.

name: Configurable step table
description: A table of steps with selectable columns (machines, belts, power, inserters, wagons, links), sortable and with precision control.
notes: observed.

name: Tree view of the chain
description: Show the chain as a collapsible hierarchy from target to raw resources.
notes: observed. Kirk's 'Add tree view' request has been open since 2019 (absence not verified in source).

name: Edit from the graph
description: Change recipe, clock, count or sloops by selecting a node in the graph.
notes: observed.

name: Persisted manual layout
description: Node positions you drag are kept across sessions, recalculations and view switches.
notes: observed. SatisfactoryTools issue (2020-11, open): manual positioning and zoom lost on tab switch.

name: Graph image export
description: Export the graph as an image (PNG/SVG) for sharing outside the tool.
notes: observed. On Ficsit Companion's wishlist; SCIM request to export the minimap view (2022, open).

name: Display units and number format
description: Choose per-second, per-minute or per-hour, and decimal precision or exact rationals.
notes: observed. Kirk can show exact rationals.

name: Command palette and search
description: Global search (Cmd+K) across game data and your own factories, jumping to the matching row.
notes: observed.

name: Localisation
description: UI strings and item, building and recipe names in many languages.
data_supported: yes — 55 locale files. Iron Plate is translated in 44 of the 54 parsed; en-*, af, et, hi, lb and vun carry English. io.json is UTF-8 while the rest are UTF-16LE, a trap for ingest.
notes: observed (planner.net reported). Modeler covers 30 languages; Factory Manager borrows SCIM catalogues. Free with our data.

name: Themes and display settings
description: Dark/light/system theme, hue, card and text size, interface scale.
notes: observed. No surveyed calculator advertises accessibility work (colour-blind palettes, keyboard-only use, screen readers). Only a colour-code helper on the wiki list does.

name: Keyboard shortcuts
description: Keyboard control for adding, linking, moving and deleting nodes.
notes: observed.

name: Guided tutorial and demo plans
description: An interactive tutorial and/or prebuilt example plans that show the tool's features.
notes: observed. Steep learning curve is Modeler's #1 complaint (reported, vaporlens).

name: In-app feedback with plan attached
description: Send a bug report or idea from inside the app, optionally attaching the plan on screen.
notes: observed (README claim).

name: New-version notice
description: Tell an open tab that a new version is live and offer a reload; refuse saves from a stale client.
notes: observed. Satisfactory Factories' API rejects writes from out-of-date clients so an old tab cannot overwrite a newer plan.

name: Installable offline app (PWA)
description: Install as an app and run without network once cached (solver, icons and data included).
notes: observed (Satisfactory Hub reported).

name: Phone-friendly layout
description: A layout designed for phones (one pane at a time, bottom bar), not just a shrunken desktop.
notes: observed for FICSIT Planner; others reported. A mobile version is requested on Modeler's forum.

name: Native desktop app
description: Downloadable desktop application with local files instead of a website.
notes: observed. Modeler adds Steam Cloud sync; reviewers prefer it to ad-supported web tools (reported).

name: Kiosk / second-screen mode
description: A view that rotates through dashboards or follows a player, meant for a side monitor.
notes: observed.

name: Codex / database browser
description: Browse items, recipes, buildings, generators, schematics with their stats and descriptions.
data_supported: yes — Docs carries display names, descriptions and stats
notes: observed (Alchemy Factory Codex reported).

name: Recipe usage lookup
description: For an item: every way to make it and everything it goes into.
notes: observed. YAFC's 'Never Enough Items' also marks which option it would choose.

name: Milestone / MAM / AWESOME Shop tracker
description: Browse and tick off milestones, MAM research and AWESOME Shop unlocks with their costs.
data_supported: yes — 574 FGSchematic typed EST_Milestone / EST_MAM / EST_ResourceSink / EST_Alternate
notes: observed (SCIM homepage).

name: Dependency explorer
description: Show what an object requires and what it unlocks, transitively.
notes: observed.

name: Per-item cost analysis
description: Give every item a cost (e.g. raw resources or logistic actions under optimal recipes) to rank recipes and items.
notes: observed (FactorioLab inferred from src/solver/item-values.ts).

name: Official data ingest pipeline
description: Generate the tool's data directly from the game's own export (Docs JSON) so updates are mechanical, not hand-entered.
data_supported: yes — this is exactly what CommunityResources Docs is
notes: observed (Satisfactory Solver's earlier read_docs.py read Docs.json; SatisfactoryMCP reads a local install's dump). Contrast Alchemy Factory, where no dump exists.

name: Game icon extraction
description: Show real item and building icons, extracted from game assets.
data_supported: partial — Docs has texture paths only (mSmallIcon); the shipped .usmap lets FModel/CUE4Parse extract them from a local install
notes: observed. Whether extracted art can be redistributed in an open-source or commercial release is a decision for Peter, not a data question.

name: Resource node map
description: An interactive world map of resource nodes, wells and geysers, filterable by resource and purity.
data_supported: no — node positions and purities are world data, not in Docs
notes: observed (Hub reported). SCIM's data is licence-locked; others extract it from the map level or community sources.

name: Collectibles map
description: Map of power slugs, hard drives, somersloops, Mercer spheres and drop pods, optionally tracking collected ones.
notes: observed (Toolbox reported).

name: Build-site ranking
description: Rank candidate sites for a factory by nearby nodes, or pick a build site for a plan.
notes: observed. Unusual.

name: World seed viewer and finder (1.2)
description: Show node layout for a 1.2 randomised world seed and search seeds for wanted resources at wanted nodes.
data_supported: no — the randomisation algorithm is not in CommunityResources
notes: observed (konsl reported). Open request on SCIM (2026-03). New in June 2026 and only a few tools have it.

name: Map measuring and annotations
description: Measure distances, drop notes or markers, filter by altitude.
notes: observed (SCIM altitude filter observed on page; markers inferred).

name: 3D factory view
description: Render a factory from the save in 3D or by floor.
data_supported: partial — needs save parsing and building meshes or footprints
notes: observed.

name: 2D layout planner
description: Place building footprints on a grid (per floor) to design a factory's physical layout.
data_supported: partial — mClearanceData gives building boxes (546 hits in Docs); port positions not verified
notes: reported (wiki listing). The calculators surveyed do not do physical layout; this is a separate tool class.

name: Generated layout or blueprint from a plan
description: Turn a solved plan into a physical layout or an importable in-game blueprint.
data_supported: partial — blueprint (.sbp) format via community parsers; footprints from mClearanceData
notes: observed (SatisfactoryMCP plan_layout/site_plan; Logistics Map blueprint export 'experimental').

name: Save upload with map overlay
description: Load a save and draw its buildings, belts, pipes, rails and vehicles on the map.
data_supported: partial — headers and .usmap help, but the save format comes from community parsers (satisfactory-file-parser, MIT)
notes: observed (Statisfactory reported).

name: Save statistics
description: Production and consumption per item, storage contents and game stats computed from a save.
notes: observed (SCIM inferred from Statistics/Game|Production|Storage modals). In-game: Factory Statistics / Factory Analytics mods.

name: Save editing
description: Modify a save and download it: move/copy/delete/rotate selections, recolour, unlock research, edit inventories, spawn miners.
data_supported: partial — needs a save writer; the parsers listed are read and write
notes: inferred from SCIM source names. A distinct product category with real corruption risk; SCIM forbids code reuse. Requests include mass-change clocks per recipe (open).

name: Auto-detect factories in a save
description: Cluster a save's machines into named factories (e.g. by belt connectivity).
notes: observed.

name: Idle and starved machine detection
description: Find machines that are stopped, starved or blocked, with the reason, and show them as a heatmap.
notes: observed. In-game: Efficiency Checker mod.

name: Upstream trace / bottleneck finder
description: From a product in your real factory, trace its supply chain upstream and find the thinnest link.
notes: observed (SatisfactoryMCP trace_upstream; Efficiency Checker in-game).

name: Power circuit analysis
description: List power circuits, their load and capacity, priority-switch break order, fuse-trip risk and unpowered machines.
data_supported: partial — needs save parser or FRM
notes: observed (SCIM inferred from Circuits/CircuitsBreakPriority modals; Power Checker mod).

name: Plan from save state
description: Plan new production using the surplus and unlocks that already exist in your save.
notes: observed.

name: Inventory and storage search
description: Find how much of an item you own and which container holds it.
data_supported: partial — needs save parser or FRM
notes: observed (SCIM Storage statistics inferred).

name: Pull save from a dedicated server
description: Fetch the latest save directly from a dedicated server (HTTPS API with admin password, or SFTP/FTP) instead of uploading by hand.
notes: observed. SCIM loads a remote URL only if the server has SSL and CORS. An admin credential is involved, so token handling and scope are a security design question.

name: Server status and admin
description: Show server state (players, tech tier, active milestone, game phase) and run admin actions (save, load, settings, restart).
data_supported: yes — QueryServerState, GetServerOptions, ApplyServerOptions, SaveGame, LoadGame, RunCommand, Shutdown; plus UDP Lightweight Query
notes: reported (wiki listing). QueryServerState gives only tech tier and active milestone, not unlocked alternates. Mostly unoccupied territory among the calculators.

name: Live factory telemetry
description: Near-real-time production rates, power, trains, vehicles and player positions from a running game.
data_supported: no — needs the FicsIt Remote Monitoring mod; the official server API does not expose production data
notes: observed. Logistics Map works without the mod at autosave cadence (about 5 minutes) and with FRM at 5 seconds.

name: Production history
description: Store production and power over time (hours to months) and chart it.
data_supported: no — needs repeated save pulls or FRM
notes: observed (SQLite; Prometheus/Postgres).

name: Alerts and notifications
description: Push alerts (e.g. a Discord webhook) on fuse trips, low battery or shortages.
notes: observed.

name: What changed since last visit
description: An overview of what is stuck now and what happened since you last looked.
notes: observed.

name: Programmatic API to plan data
description: Expose plans or factory data to other programs (remote interface, HTTP API, MCP).
notes: observed. Factorio mods expose Lua remote interfaces; SatisfactoryMCP exposes 49 MCP tools.

name: Natural-language / LLM interface
description: Ask questions or request plans in plain language and have a model call the planner.
notes: observed (SatisfactoryMCP); reported ('AI Architect' in Satisfied Planner 2).

name: In-game planner
description: The planner runs inside the game as a mod UI, with access to live unlock state.
data_supported: no — would need a Satisfactory mod (SML), outside CommunityResources
notes: observed. No Satisfactory equivalent found (ficsit.app lookup returned none for the obvious references). Ficsit Companion lists it as an idea.

name: In-game throughput instruments
description: Mod buildings or HUDs that measure actual belt throughput and machine efficiency in game.
notes: observed (Throughput Counter, Efficiency Checker, Factory Analytics). Complements rather than competes with a calculator.

name: URL-encoded sharing
description: The entire plan is encoded into a link, with no server storage; opening the link reproduces it.
notes: observed. Zero hosting cost and privacy-preserving, but links get long (Alchemy calc plans bit-packing).

name: Server-hosted snapshot link
description: Upload a frozen copy of the plan and get a short link; the copy does not change when you keep editing.
notes: observed. Satisfactory Factories mints one link per plan version and keeps it separate from the live-invite link.

name: Live collaborative editing
description: Several people edit the same plan at once with changes synced live, presence shown and conflicts resolved.
notes: observed (Satisfactory Architect inferred from sync/ source). Satisfactory Factories: rooms by slug, optional password, per-field edit locks, guard against mass deletion.

name: Shared-plan permissions
description: Per-person rights on a shared plan (viewer vs editor; read/write/delete), with revocation.
notes: observed. Helmod does this in-game for Factorio multiplayer; SatisfactoryBase invites viewers or editors; Satisfactory Factories uses a password and an owner 'stop sharing'.

name: Accounts and cross-device sync
description: Sign in and have plans follow you across devices.
notes: observed. Logins: Discord/Google (Satisfactory Logistics), Steam Cloud (Modeler).

name: No account required
description: Full functionality without signing up; data stays in the browser or on disk.
notes: observed. A design stance: accounts are additive, never a gate.

name: Offline editing with conflict resolution
description: Keep editing a synced plan offline and, on reconnect, see a prompt listing every conflicting change to choose from.
notes: observed. The prompt survives a page refresh, after a bug where refresh silently picked one side.

name: File export and import
description: Save a plan to a file (JSON or a custom format) and load it back or send it to someone.
notes: observed. SatisfactoryTools exports '.sft' (2026-03).

name: Import from another tool
description: Read another planner's export format to migrate plans.
notes: observed (SatisfactoryTools .txt import, v0.7). The only cross-tool interop found.

name: Named local saved plans
description: Keep several named plans or presets in the browser and switch between them.
notes: observed.

name: Community gallery
description: Browse and publish other players' plans or in-game blueprints.
notes: observed (SCIM about 4,938 blueprints and 467 megaprints); blueprint repositories reported.

name: Shared-text safety rules
description: Validate user text in shared plans (no links or markup, length limits) on client and server, and repair old data.
notes: observed. Arose from an XSS-class bug: tooltips rendered plan text as raw HTML (fixed). Any shared or collaborative feature inherits this.

name: Anonymous usage telemetry
description: Count usage (tabs, plan sizes, feature use) without accounts, to know how the tool is used.
notes: observed (six numbers and one flag; searched terms not sent). Relevant to Peter's observability value.

name: Multiple games in one tool
description: One app with per-game data packs and a game switcher.
notes: observed. FactorioLab covers about 15 games through one generic schema (items, recipes, machines, belts, fuels, modules). dsp-calc-opt switches between DSP mod datasets.

name: Custom game data editor
description: Define an entirely new game's items, recipes and machines inside the tool, then share it.
notes: observed (FactorioLab editor and 'Custom' game).

name: Sell value and profit
description: Compute what a chain costs to run and what its output sells for.
data_supported: partial — Satisfactory has no money; AWESOME Sink points are the analogue
notes: observed. Core to Alchemy Factory, a shop and economy game.

name: Secondary resource budgets
description: Track non-item quantities a chain produces or consumes: heat, nutrients, pollution, net heat value.
notes: observed (Alchemy heat and nutrients; FactorioLab pollution; dsp-calc-opt min net heat).

name: Footprint estimate
description: Estimate the floor area the plan's buildings occupy.
data_supported: partial — mClearanceData bounding boxes per building
notes: observed. No Satisfactory planner surveyed shows it, though Docs could drive an approximation.

name: World seed statistics (non-Satisfactory)
description: Query a procedural world seed for resource availability and feed it into the plan.
notes: observed (DSP seed viewer with statistics and confidence intervals). The Satisfactory 1.2 analogue is the world seed finder row.

name: Customisation helpers
description: Colour code converters and palette tools for in-game painting.
data_supported: partial — FGCustomizationRecipe (106) present; colour values not checked
notes: observed (SCIM colour converter). Off-core.

name: World leaderboards
description: Compare progress or production across uploaded saves.
notes: observed (homepage link). Rare; depends on collecting saves.
